textbookText: 121. For a concave mirror, using the Cartesian sign convention, the focal length is taken as: A) Negative, since it lies on the same side as the incident light (in front of the mirror) B) Positive, since it lies behind the mirror C) Zero always D) Equal to the radius of curvature exactly
122. The relation between focal length (f) and radius of curvature (R) of a spherical mirror is: A) f = R/2 B) f = 2R C) f = R D) f = R/4

123. A concave mirror forms a real, inverted, diminished image when the object is placed: A) Beyond the centre of curvature (C) B) At the focus (F) C) Between the pole and focus D) At the centre of curvature exactly

124. A convex mirror always forms an image that is: A) Virtual, erect, and diminished, regardless of object position B) Real and inverted for distant objects C) Real and magnified when the object is near D) Inverted and diminished
125. The mirror formula relating object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) is: A) 1/v + 1/u = 1/f B) 1/v − 1/u = 1/f C) v + u = f D) vu = f

126. Why are convex mirrors used as rear-view/side mirrors in vehicles (application-based fact)? A) They give an erect, diminished image with a wider field of view than a plane mirror of the same size B) They magnify distant objects for better clarity C) They form real images that can be projected on a screen D) They invert the image to correct driver perception

127. When an object is placed exactly at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror, the image formed is: A) Real, inverted, and of the same size as the object B) Virtual, erect, and magnified C) Real, inverted, and magnified D) At infinity

128. Concave mirrors are used in torches and headlights because they: A) Placed with source at focus, produce a parallel (collimated) reflected beam B) Diverge light rays to spread illumination widely C) Always produce virtual images that appear brighter D) Absorb light to prevent glare
129. Linear magnification (m) for a spherical mirror is given by: A) m = −v/u B) m = v/u only, always positive C) m = f/u D) m = u/f

130. An object placed between the pole and focus of a concave mirror produces an image that is: A) Virtual, erect, and magnified — as used in a shaving/makeup mirror B) Real, inverted, and diminished C) Real and located between C and F D) Virtual and diminished

131. Which is an extraordinary/unusual application of a concave mirror in medicine? A) The dentist's/ENT mirror gives a magnified, erect view of small areas like teeth when the object is within the focal length B) It is used only for making objects appear farther away C) It is used to disperse light into a spectrum D) It cannot be used at close distances at all

132. A ray of light parallel to the principal axis, after reflecting from a concave mirror, passes through: A) The principal focus B) The centre of curvature C) The pole of the mirror D) Infinity, remaining parallel

133. A ray passing through the centre of curvature of a spherical mirror, after reflection: A) Retraces its own path back through C (since it strikes the mirror normally) B) Passes through the focus instead C) Becomes parallel to the principal axis D) Is completely absorbed by the mirror

134. For a concave mirror, when the object is at infinity, the image is formed: A) At the focus, real, inverted, and highly diminished (point-sized) B) At the centre of curvature, virtual and magnified C) Behind the mirror, virtual D) At the pole of the mirror

135. Solar cookers commonly use concave (parabolic) mirrors because they: A) Converge parallel sunlight to a focal point, concentrating heat energy there B) Diverge sunlight to cover a wider cooking area C) Reflect sunlight without any convergence D) Absorb sunlight instead of reflecting it
136. The power of a mirror is related to its focal length by: A) P = 1/f (in metres), analogous to lens power B) P = f, directly C) P = f², directly D) P = 2f

137. A dentist's mirror is typically: A) Concave, to give a magnified virtual image of teeth when held close B) Convex, to give a magnified image C) Plane, to give a life-size image only D) Convex, to diminish the image for a wider view

138. For a convex mirror, the image distance (v) is always: A) Positive (image forms behind the mirror, virtual) B) Negative (image forms in front of the mirror, real) C) Zero regardless of object position D) Equal to the object distance always
139. According to sign convention, distances measured against the direction of incident light are taken as: A) Negative B) Positive C) Zero D) Undefined

140. A concave mirror produces a virtual, erect, and magnified image ONLY when the object is: A) Placed between the pole and the focus B) Placed beyond the centre of curvature C) Placed exactly at the centre of curvature D) Placed at infinity
